possible_confounders: Respiratory rate and depth during recording
Recent caffeine, nicotine, or alcohol use
control_variables: Age, sex, BMI
VO2max or validated fitness proxy
Paced breathing protocol (0.25 Hz) during baseline and stress
12-hour caffeine/alcohol abstinence, nicotine abstinence
Medication-free inclusion criterion
Sessions scheduled at same circadian phase (±1h)
Standardized sensor placement with photographic verification
boring_rival_explanations: Variation in stressor adherence/compliance masquerades as ANS phenotype effects
Skin-sensor interface differences (H2) correlate with ANS phenotype and drive SNR variation
Regression to the mean in extreme baseline RMSSD groups creates spurious U-shaped AUC relationship
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If stressor non-adherence drives the effect, high-baseline-RMSSD subjects with low AUC will show blunted cortisol reactivity to the stressor; if ANS phenotype drives it, they will show normal cortisol reactivity but compressed HRV dynamic range.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Concurrent salivary cortisol sampling during stress sessions: observe whether low-AUC high-RMSSD subjects have attenuated cortisol AUCg (supports non-adherence) or normal cortisol AUCg with reduced ΔRMSSD (supports ANS mechanism).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Cortisol provides orthogonal stress-system readout unaffected by HRV dynamic range compression. Must control for cortisol sampling timing relative to stressor onset.

possible_confounders: Ambient light leakage into PPG sensor
control_variables: Light-tight sensor housing or dark room
Climate-controlled room (22±1°C, 40-60% RH)
Standardized strap tension via spring-loaded clasp
Seated, minimal-movement protocol with accelerometer gating
Dermatological screening exclusion
Skin cleaning protocol (alcohol wipe, 5-min dry)
Single device model/batch; cross-over sensor swap design
boring_rival_explanations: Signal quality differences stem from device manufacturing variability, not subject anatomy
Motion artifact (H5) dominates noise floor; static anatomy measures are epiphenomenal
Software filtering pipeline introduces subject-dependent artifacts via fixed parameters
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If device variability drives noise floors, swapping sensors between subjects will transfer the signal quality profile (SQI, impedance) to the new subject; if anatomy drives it, the profile stays with the subject.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Cross-over design: each subject wears 3 different sensors (same model) in counterbalanced order; compute intraclass correlation (ICC) of PPG SQI and EDA impedance partitioned by subject vs. sensor. Subject ICC > 0.6 and sensor ICC < 0.2 supports anatomy mechanism.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Requires identical sensor firmware and filtering. Sensor order randomization controls for session-order effects. Measure impedance at 10 Hz before/after each session.

control_variables: Actigraphy-verified sleep schedule (7-9h, fixed bed/wake) for 7 days prior
Caffeine abstinence 12h pre-session
Controlled light exposure (dim light <10 lux pre-session, standardized bright light pulse)
Menstrual phase tracking; test in early follicular or control hormonally
Counterbalanced season enrollment
Forced desynchrony or constant routine to dissociate circadian phase from time awake
Identical stressor protocol at all circadian phases
boring_rival_explanations: Detection uncertainty follows time-awake fatigue monotonically, not circadian phase
Signal quality (H2, H7) degrades at night due to temperature/movement, not physiology
Stressor effectiveness varies by time-of-day (e.g., social stress less potent at night)
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If fatigue drives uncertainty, AUC will decline linearly with hours awake regardless of chronotype; if circadian gain modulation drives it, AUC will track circadian phase (e.g., nadir near CBTmin) with chronotype-dependent phase shift.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Forced desynchrony protocol (28h day) with stress tests at 6+ circadian phases: regress session AUC on circadian phase (hours from DLMO) and time awake; significant circadian phase × chronotype interaction with non-significant time-awake effect supports mechanism.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Forced desynchrony is gold standard but expensive; constant routine with 4+ phases is minimum viable. Must measure DLMO via hourly saliva melatonin in dim light.

possible_confounders: Cultural differences in extreme vs. moderate response style
Momentary distraction or multitasking during response
Social desirability bias varying by context
EMA prompt timing relative to stressor offset
Device usability issues (screen size, notification fatigue)
control_variables: Standardized EMA training session with practice trials
Simple 0-100 VAS with anchors; avoid Likert scales
Compliance monitoring with real-time feedback
Prompt randomization within windows; exclude responses >5 min after prompt
Include infrequency/validity scales in EMA battery
Fixed prompt-stressor latency (e.g., prompt at stressor offset + 2 min)
Usability testing; provide dedicated study phone
boring_rival_explanations: Label noise is context-dependent (e.g., higher variance at work) not trait-dependent
Physiological measures are the noisy channel; EMA labels are accurate
Traits correlate with physiology but labeling is unbiased; confounding is illusory
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If label noise is context-dependent, within-subject EMA variance will correlate with context (work vs. leisure) but not with TAS-20 or interoceptive accuracy; if trait-dependent, variance will correlate with traits across contexts.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Multilevel model: EMA stress rating ~ physiology + context + TAS-20 + (1|subject). Significant TAS-20 × physiology interaction predicting rating residual supports trait mechanism; significant context × physiology interaction without trait effect supports context rival.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Ground-truth calibration requires laboratory stressor with known onset. Use that to quantify each subject's labeling bias (EMA - physiology) and test if bias correlates with traits.

possible_confounders: Sensor placement tightness and location variability
Concurrent physiological changes (vasoconstriction) altering PPG-optical coupling
control_variables: Standardized placement with 3D-printed guide; tightness via calibrated strap
Single device model, locked firmware
Fixed filter pipeline (e.g., wavelet denoising with universal thresholds)
Video-verified activity labels for ≥20% of wear time
Simultaneous impedance plethysmography to track vasoconstriction
Exclude vehicle/machinery exposure via GPS + accelerometer
Wear on bare skin; standardized clothing protocol
boring_rival_explanations: Residual artifact after filtering is universally high in HRV band, not subject-specific
Stress itself increases fidgeting/movement, creating stress-correlated artifact
Artifact spectral overlap is random across subjects; no consistent profile
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If stress-induced movement drives artifact, motion power in HRV band will increase during stress epochs regardless of activity type; if subject-specific movement profile drives it, artifact spectrum will be stable within activity type across stress/non-stress.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Compare accelerometer-PPG coherence in 0.1-0.4 Hz band during stress vs. non-stress epochs matched for activity label (e.g., sitting). Significant stress × activity interaction on coherence supports stress-movement rival; stable coherence per activity supports subject-specific profile.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Requires precise activity labeling. Use video annotation for subset to validate self-report. Compute subject-specific artifact templates per activity; test if template-matched filtering reduces HRV error more than generic filtering.

possible_confounders: Stressor similarity (e.g., two cognitive tasks) inflating stereotypy
Measurement noise (H2, H5) masquerading as low stereotypy
Sensor drift across sessions (H7) altering feature distributions
Learning effects improving classifier performance over sessions
Baseline feature variance differences, not response consistency
control_variables: Stressors from distinct domains: social-evaluative (TSST), physical (cold pressor), cognitive (mental arithmetic)
Counterbalanced stressor order across subjects
Sensor calibration check before each session; exclude drifted sessions
Minimum 5 sessions per stressor type
Controlled lab environment, same time-of-day
Include non-stress baseline sessions to estimate measurement noise floor
Compute stereotypy on residualized features (remove session mean)
boring_rival_explanations: Stereotypy reflects stressor similarity, not a subject trait
Low stereotypy is due to high measurement noise, not true physiological variability
Sample complexity differences stem from baseline feature variance, not response consistency
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If stereotypy is stressor-specific, within-subject response correlation will be high for similar stressors (e.g., TSST vs. speech) but low across domains; if a trait, correlation will be high across all domain pairs.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Compute within-subject stress response vectors (Δfeatures) for each stressor; calculate pairwise correlations across all stressor pairs. High mean correlation across domain-dissimilar pairs (e.g., TSST vs cold pressor) supports trait mechanism; high only within domain supports stressor similarity.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Use participation ratio of PCA eigenvalues on concatenated stress-response vectors. Must ensure stressors elicit comparable subjective stress (EMA-matched) to avoid intensity confounds.

possible_confounders: Battery voltage sag affecting LED current
Non-wear periods misclassified as signal loss
Subject removing device during high-stress contexts
Skin chemistry changes (pH, microbiome) unrelated to sweat
control_variables: New devices from single production batch
Standardized storage (22°C, 40% RH, light-tight)
Firmware locked; no OTA updates during study
Battery monitoring; replace at 3.0V threshold
Wear detection via skin temperature + capacitance; distinguish non-wear from poor signal
Daily self-check: 30-sec reference recording at wake/sleep
Sweat patch pH at wrist weekly; skin microbiome swabs monthly
boring_rival_explanations: Drift is random (Brownian) and not exposure-dependent
Missingness during stress is due to subject non-wear (removal), not signal corruption
Drift correlates with calendar time, not cumulative exposure
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If missingness is non-wear, wear-detection sensors (skin temp, capacitance) will show off-body signature during gaps; if drift-induced signal loss, wear sensors show on-body but PPG/EDA quality metrics (SQI, impedance) plummet.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Little's MCAR test on missingness pattern stratified by wear-detection state. Reject MCAR for on-body poor-quality segments during high-stress-context exposure (heat >30°C, exertion >3 METs) but not for off-body segments supports drift mechanism.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Must validate wear-detection algorithm against ground-truth (video). Track cumulative exposure metrics: sweat pH (patch), UV (dosimeter), mechanical RMS (accelerometer). Drift rate = slope of weekly reference impedance/amplitude.

possible_confounders: Sensor placement pressure altering local hemodynamics
Sympathetic outflow differences (not anatomy) driving peripheral signals
control_variables: Age-stratified recruitment (18-30, 31-45, 46-60)
Normotensive, medication-free (washout 2 weeks if ethical)
Standardized hydration (500mL water 2h pre-session)
Thermoneutral room (23±1°C), skin temp clamped via water-perfused cuff
Supine position, arm supported at heart level
3D-printed sensor mount with fixed pressure (20 mmHg)
Direct MSNA recording (microneurography) for central outflow ground truth
boring_rival_explanations: Peripheral signal differences reflect sympathetic outflow heterogeneity, not vascular anatomy
Anatomy correlates with age; age drives both anatomy and transfer function
Sensor placement variability creates apparent transfer function differences
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If sympathetic outflow differences drive peripheral signals, MSNA burst pattern will predict peripheral waveform dynamics better than anatomical measures; if anatomy drives it, anatomical measures will predict transfer function gain/latency after controlling for MSNA.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Simultaneous MSNA + wearable recording during TSST. Fit subject-specific transfer function (MSNA → PPG amplitude, PTT, temp, EDA). Multiple regression: transfer function gain ~ cfPWV + capillary density + venous compliance + MSNA burst frequency. Significant anatomy coefficients after MSNA control supports mechanism.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: MSNA is invasive; limit to n≈20. Alternative: pharmacological stressor (yohimbine) with known central effect. Must measure cfPWV (tonometry), capillary density (nailfold videomicroscopy), venous compliance (occlusion plethysmography).

possible_confounders: Personality traits (neuroticism, extraversion) correlating with appraisal
control_variables: Standardized TSST with challenge/threat manipulation (resource evaluation instructions)
Naive to TSST; no prior lab stress exposure
No social support during stressor; experimenter blind to condition
Measure and covary neuroticism (BFI-2), extraversion
Coping inventory (COPE) as covariate
VO2max measurement; exclude beta-blockers/CV meds
Impedance cardiography for CO/TPR ground truth
boring_rival_explanations: Physiological differences reflect fitness/health status, not appraisal style
Appraisal is epiphenomenal; physiology drives appraisal (reverse causality)
Classifier misalignment stems from inadequate feature set, not appraisal mediation
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If physiology drives appraisal, manipulating physiology (e.g., acute beta-blockade) will alter challenge/threat ratings; if appraisal drives physiology, manipulating appraisal instructions will alter CO/TPR pattern without changing fitness.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Randomized crossover: same TSST with challenge vs threat instructions (counterbalanced). Measure CO/TPR and wearable features. Significant instruction × appraisal style interaction on CO/TPR (challenge instructions → higher CO/TPR ratio in challenge-appraisers) supports appraisal mechanism.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Appraisal style measured via pre-stressor resource/demand evaluation (Tomaka scale). Challenge = resources > demands; threat = demands > resources. Must verify manipulation check (post-stressor appraisal rating).

possible_confounders: Insufficient within-subject data (low N per subject) causing estimation error
Model misspecification (non-Gaussian random effects, non-linear dynamics)
Non-stationarity within subject (changing dynamics over study)
Outlier subjects with poor data quality (artifact, non-wear)
EMA label noise (H4) inflating within-subject variance
control_variables: Intensive longitudinal design: ≥60 days, ≥10 stress events, ≥5 EMA/day
Model checking: posterior predictive checks, LOO-CV, prior sensitivity analysis
Stationarity tests (KPSS, rolling AR coefficients) per subject
Data quality flags: exclude sessions with >20% artifact, non-wear >2h
Weakly informative priors; compare to flat priors
Stressor alignment via physiological onset (HRV drop) not EMA timestamp
Use laboratory-calibrated stress labels for subset to quantify EMA noise
boring_rival_explanations: Apparent non-ergodicity is due to low within-subject sample size (estimation error)
Hierarchical model miscalibration stems from prior misspecification, not true non-ergodicity
Outlier subjects have systematically poorer signal quality, not different dynamics
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If non-ergodicity is due to low within-subject N, increasing N (via longer monitoring or more stressors) will reduce shrinkage bias for outlier subjects; if true non-ergodicity, bias persists even with large N.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Subsample within-subject data at increasing N (5, 10, 20, 40 stress events); plot hierarchical model calibration error (ECE) vs N for subjects in tails of slope distribution (|z|>2). Persistent ECE gap at N=40 supports non-ergodicity; convergence supports estimation-error rival.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Requires very long monitoring. Alternative: simulate data from known non-ergodic (mixture of dynamical systems) vs ergodic (hierarchical Gaussian) generative models; test if hierarchical model recovers true parameters. Real-data test needs ≥50 subjects with dense sampling.
